LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableSystem_Tip: Master switch. When off, no news arrives, no ripples apply, and the News tab is hidden. Existing save data is preserved.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_Plague_Tip: Allow plague outbreaks to be generated as news events in neighboring factions.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_Coup_Tip: Allow coup attempts to be generated in neighboring factions, with goodwill shifts on resolution.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_War_Tip: Allow inter-faction wars to be generated, optionally affecting trade routes (see War trade disruption below).
LanguageData.TN_Settings_FactionSim_Tip: Give factions living relations, leader legitimacy, and internal entropy. When on, the news the world generates is driven by these meters and each leader's personality (unstable leaders get couped, hostile neighbors go to war, friendly ones ally) instead of being purely random. When off, events are selected at random as before.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_Fragmentation_Tip: Allow factions whose internal entropy runs out of control to fracture - a breakaway region splits off and a settlement may be abandoned. Requires Faction simulation.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_RealisticWars_Tip: Model wars as a series of battles - relative strength, shifting momentum, and mounting exhaustion decide an actual victor instead of a symmetric armistice. A decisive defeat heavily destabilizes the loser and can cascade (via Faction simulation) into a coup or fragmentation. When off, wars use the legacy goodwill-driven progression.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_Coalitions_Tip: When one faction grows into an over-mighty, aggressive hegemon, the threatened powers band together into a coalition and declare war on it - a self-correcting balance of power. Requires Realistic wars.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_DiplomaticDoctrines_Tip: Each faction follows an evolving foreign-policy doctrine (isolationist, pragmatic, expansionist, hegemonic, revanchist) derived from its leader, power, and history. The doctrine steers who it fights and who it courts, and is reported when it shifts. Requires Faction simulation.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_TreatyNetwork_Tip: Factions sign typed treaties (non-aggression, defensive pacts, trade pacts, vassalage) and can betray them - a backstab that becomes a casus belli and craters the betrayer's standing with the rest of the world. Requires Faction simulation.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_WarEscalation_Tip: Wars no longer erupt overnight. Rivalries simmer through grievance, ultimatum, and mobilization, with real off-ramps - bilateral de-escalation, third-party mediation, or backing down against a coalition - so some crises are defused without a shot. Requires Faction simulation.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_DiplomaticCrises_Tip: Border incidents, embargoes, arms races, and envoy expulsions occur between rivals - friction that builds pressure toward (or away from) open war without committing to it. Requires the war escalation ladder.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_BlocsPolarity_Tip: Alliance networks crystallize into named, persistent blocs, and the balance of power resolves into a world polarity (fragmented, unipolar, bipolar, multipolar) that shifts global war and coalition pressure. Requires Faction simulation.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_SuccessionDiplomacy_Tip: Leadership crises can be contested by a foreign-backed pretender, and the new regime's recognition by other factions shapes its legitimacy and alignments. Requires Faction simulation.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_StateOfWorldDigest_Tip: A periodic foreign-affairs analysis piece synthesizing the geopolitical picture - rising and falling powers, blocs, rivalries, and world polarity. Requires an active radio receiver and the Diplomatic Corps research; its depth grows with deployed diplomats.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_TechEras: Technological eras and the tech-leak race
LanguageData.TN_Settings_TechEras_Tip: Factions accrue research toward breakthroughs that raise their war strength and standing. A faction that falls behind catches up faster through espionage and arms races, so a leader's edge erodes over time. Falling two generations behind stokes revanchist pressure. Requires faction simulation.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_ProsperityCycles_Tip: Each faction's economy cycles between boom and bust, dragged down by wars, embargoes, and famine. Prosperity feeds a faction's power ranking and ability to expand, and a deep bust can push a desperate leader toward a diversionary war. Requires faction simulation.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_FamineBorderPressure_Tip: When famine or catastrophe empties a city, the exodus strains the stricken faction's nearest neighbour weeks later - souring relations and stoking unrest that can topple a domino of its own. It never destroys the neighbour's settlements, only pressures them. Requires faction simulation.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_ProxyWars_Tip: A non-belligerent rival may secretly arm one side of a war, lengthening it. The sponsorship is reported as a rumor you can verify; a confirmed proxy gives the wronged side fresh cause for war, while a fabricated rumor is debunked. Requires faction simulation and war events.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_ResourceEconomy: Resource economy: shocks and resource wars
LanguageData.TN_Settings_ResourceEconomy_Tip: Each faction has a commodity it exports and one it depends on, and can fall into a shortage or a glut of food, medicine, metals, textiles, weapons, or luxuries. Shocks move that faction's trade prices for the affected goods (sell into a shortage at a premium, buy a glut cheap), nudge its prosperity, and surface in the feed. A power chronically starved of what a hoarding neighbour controls can slide into a resource war. Requires faction simulation.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_MarketsWire_Tip: Once per quadrum, the markets desk posts a synthesized economic briefing to the feed - the sharpest price movers, commodities under shock, contagion, and the standout booms and busts. Requires an active radio receiver and the World Comms Protocols research. Needs the resource economy enabled.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableThreads_Tip: Allow multi-stage story arcs (e.g. War: Tension → Open Conflict → Stalemate → Peace Talks). Without this, only one-off news items are generated.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableVerify_Tip: Allow the player to verify rumors via the Comms Console. False rumors produce correction items when resolved.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableAlerts_Tip: Master switch for delivery-time notifications. When off, news arrives silently in the console only.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableRadioUnstaffedAlert: Warn when radio receiver is unstaffed
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableRadioUnstaffedAlert_Ti: Show the alert when a radio receiver is online with automatic radio watch on but nobody is monitoring it. Turn off if you prefer to staff receivers manually without the reminder.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableLetters_Tip: Allow subscription alerts to use full letters. When off, alerts set to 'Letter' downgrade to message-bar messages.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableCorrections_Tip: When a verify-false rumor resolves, generate a correction item in the news console. Disabling suppresses the correction item entirely.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableStagedThreads_Tip: Allow story arcs to advance through their full stage sequence and resolve. When off, threads stop after stage 1.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnablePrisonerInterrogationI: Allow interrogated prisoners to yield foreign-desk intel about their faction's ongoing crises.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableCovOps_Tip: Enable covert operations (plant false cause, sow discord). Has per-faction cooldowns.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableColonistReactions_Tip: Colonists passively react to ongoing wars, plagues, and alliances every few days via thoughts.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableHomelandTies_Tip: Each colonist is tied to a homeland faction (refugees keep the one they fled). Confirmed news about that faction hits them personally - grief for a catastrophe, pride for an alliance, relief when bad news is retracted - and harder if they heard it at the receiver. Mood only.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableDividedHouse_Tip: An unverified rumor splits the colony - some colonists take it to heart, others scoff - instead of everyone reacting the same way. Stance leans on temperament. Mood only.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableLongDread_Tip: A major foreign crisis that drags on unresolved wears on the colony's mood the longer it simmers, with a wave of relief when it finally ends. Mood only.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableDiplomatDispatches_Tip: Active diplomats periodically send field reports into the news feed.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableConflictCauses_Tip: Tag wars / coups / plagues with specific causes (drought, blockade, succession, etc). Drives narrative variety and the credibility-challenge system.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableWarRipple_Tip: Wars between neighboring factions can disrupt their trade caravans to your colony and apply embargo price multipliers.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnablePlagueRipple_Tip: While a plague is active in a faction, their visitors and traders may arrive carrying Flu hediffs.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableCrisisScarcity_Tip: Caravans arriving from a plague-stricken faction bring less food and medicine; caravans arriving during a regional famine bring less food.

Build a radio receiver, keep it powered and switched on, and place it in an enclosed room. LanguageData.TN_Alert_RadioReceiverOffline_Desc_VFE: Radio Monitoring has been researched, but the colony has no usable receiver. Power a radio (industrial or longwave), switch it on, and place it in an enclosed room. Without reception, long-range reports arrive slowly and with lower reliability; traveler reports can still appear.
LanguageData.TN_Alert_RadioReceiverUnstaffed_Desc: A radio receiver is online and set to automatic radio watch, but nobody is monitoring it. Assign a hearing-capable colonist with Intellectual work available to Research work, disable automatic watch on that receiver, or right-click it and prioritize monitoring to improve report speed and reliability.
LanguageData.TN_Alert_CommsConsoleOffline_Desc: World Comms Protocols has been researched, but the colony has no powered comms console. Build or power a comms console to send aid, request briefings, verify reports, and run diplomatic operations.

LanguageData.TN_Alert_PublicHealthPreparednessThin_De: An outside outbreak is active, but the colony has no current health advisory for at least one affected faction or has fewer than 12 stored medicine. Issue a Health Advisory from the News Console and stock medicine to reduce illness spillover from visitors and caravans.

LanguageData.TN_InfoPosture_OpenBriefings_Tooltip: Open briefings: confirmed reports spread confidence faster and slightly improve collection, but public discussion can also carry rumors farther.
LanguageData.TN_InfoPosture_RumorControl_Tooltip: Rumor control: analysts suppress unverified claims and misleading chatter, reducing colony discussion while slightly improving report reliability.
LanguageData.TN_InfoPosture_RadioSilence_Tooltip: Radio silence: the colony limits public discussion. Rumors fade quickly, but useful confidence and traveler/caravan intel suffer.

LanguageData.TN_CovOp_SeedAlliance_Success_Story: Your covert brokering helped frame the terms. Both factions are now exchanging envoys through unofficial channels. If the story advances, a formal alliance announcement may follow. Your colony gains modest goodwill with both parties.
LanguageData.TN_CovOp_SeedAlliance_Blown_Body: Your attempt to quietly broker an agreement between {0} and {1} was revealed, undermining the operation.
LanguageData.TN_CovOp_SeedAlliance_Blown_Story: One of the factions disclosed the back-channel approach. The exposed mediation effort has made {0} less receptive to your influence for the time being.
LanguageData.TN_CovOp_SabotageTradeRoute_Success_Body: Interference with {0}'s logistical network has disrupted caravan and trade route schedules for an estimated {1} days.
LanguageData.TN_CovOp_SabotageTradeRoute_Success_Stor: The disruption appears to be holding. Merchants are rerouting and {0}-linked caravans are running irregular schedules. Monitor the situation - disruption may affect your own trade opportunities if {0} is a major partner.
LanguageData.TN_CovOp_SabotageTradeRoute_Blown_Headli: Trade sabotage attributed to your colony - {0} responds
LanguageData.TN_CovOp_SabotageTradeRoute_Blown_Body: {0} has publicly blamed your colony for a deliberate attack on their trade routes.
LanguageData.TN_CovOp_SabotageTradeRoute_Blown_Story: The sabotage was traced and attributed. {0} is likely to respond through diplomatic or trade pressure. The incident will damage your standing with trade-linked factions in the region.
LanguageData.TN_Letter_WarBreaks_Text: Intelligence reports confirm that {0} and {1} have entered open conflict. The fighting may affect trade routes, visitors, and faction relations in your region.
LanguageData.TN_Letter_PlagueConfirmed_Text: An outbreak has been confirmed in {0}. Visitors from that faction may carry illness. Consider preparing medical supplies and screening arrivals carefully.
LanguageData.TN_Letter_AllianceSigned_Text: {0} and {1} have signed a formal alliance. This may improve trade access and regional stability - or draw your colony into their affairs.
LanguageData.TN_Letter_CoupResolved_Text: The political crisis in {0} has resolved. A new leadership is in control. Their posture toward outside parties - including your colony - may have changed.
LanguageData.TN_AllianceDefenseFund_Body: {0} sends {1} silver as part of the mutual defense pact. Shared security comes with shared costs - and shared benefits.
LanguageData.TN_AllianceResourceGift_Body: {0} delivers {1} {2} as part of the resource sharing agreement. The alliance is already paying dividends.
LanguageData.TN_RefugeeRequest_Plague_Body: A group of {0} survivors led by {1} has arrived at the edge of the colony, fleeing the outbreak in {2}. They ask for shelter. What will you do?
LanguageData.TN_RefugeeRequest_War_Body: A group of {0} survivors led by {1} has traveled from the conflict in {2}. They are unarmed and ask only to stay. What will you do?
LanguageData.TN_RefugeeRequest_Env_Body: A group of {0} people led by {1} has fled the disaster in {2}, their land left unlivable. They are unarmed and ask only to stay and work. What will you do?
LanguageData.TN_RefugeeRequest_Famine_Body: A group of {0} starving families led by {1} has reached the colony from {2}. The famine has emptied their stores. They beg for food and a place to stay. What will you do?
LanguageData.TN_Refugee_AcceptedMsg: {0} and the group of {1} survivors are welcomed into the colony.
LanguageData.TN_RefugeeArrived_Body: {0} and the survivors from {2} have reached the colony and joined as a group. {1} speaks for them, and they are ready to work.
LanguageData.TN_RefugeeGuest_Body: {0} survivors led by {1} settle in as guests from {2}. They will live and work alongside the colony for about {3} days, then move on - though some may grow attached and ask to stay for good.
LanguageData.TN_RefugeeGuest_DepartBody: The refugee guests' stay has ended. {0} chose to stay and join the colony for good; {1} thanked the colony and moved on.
LanguageData.TN_Refugee_RefusedMsg: {0}s group was turned away. They left quietly, but the decision weighs on people.
LanguageData.TN_Refugee_GiveFood: Give them {0} meals and send them on
LanguageData.TN_Refugee_GiveFood_Disabled: Not enough food in storage to spare.
LanguageData.TN_Refugee_GaveFoodMsg: {0}s group of {1} take {2} meals and move on. They will not forget the gesture.
LanguageData.TN_NearbyPlague_ColonistSick: {0} has come down with an illness. The ongoing outbreak in a nearby faction may be a factor.
LanguageData.TN_Letter_WarPeaceTalks_Text: Negotiations have reportedly begun between {0} and {1}. The fighting may wind down, but terms are still being debated and the outcome is uncertain.
LanguageData.TN_Letter_WarArmistice_Text: The conflict between {0} and {1} has ended with a signed armistice. Trade routes are reopening and the region should stabilize.
LanguageData.TN_Letter_PlagueSubsiding_Text: The outbreak in {0} appears to be under control. Quarantine lines are relaxing and the immediate health risk to the region is diminishing.
LanguageData.TN_Letter_CoupAttempt_Text: A coup attempt is underway in {0}. The outcome is uncertain and the faction may emerge with very different leadership - and very different policies toward your colony.
LanguageData.TN_Pending_Tip: This report has not yet arrived. It will be delivered when the news reaches the colony.
LanguageData.TN_Alert_WarNearby_Desc: An active military conflict is underway between factions near your colony. Trade routes are disrupted, prices are elevated, and the fighting may spill over. Monitor the News Console for updates.
LanguageData.TN_Alert_FamineNearby_Desc: A food crisis has been reported in a nearby faction. Food prices at local traders are elevated. Displaced wanderers may approach the colony seeking shelter.
LanguageData.TN_Thought_EspionageNearby_Desc: A foreign spy network was uncovered near our colony. Who else might be watching?
LanguageData.TN_Thought_EconomicCrisisNearby_Desc: A nearby faction's economy has collapsed. Prices are rising and supply chains are disrupted.
LanguageData.TN_Thought_TechBreakthroughInspired_Desc: Word of a nearby technological breakthrough has sparked fresh ideas and optimism.
LanguageData.TN_Thought_CultRiseUnsettling_Desc: A fanatical movement is spreading through the region. Its influence feels uncomfortably close.
LanguageData.TN_Thought_PirateRaidFear_Desc: Coordinated pirates are hitting trade routes nearby. Our colony could be next.
LanguageData.TN_Thought_AncientSiteWonder_Desc: Pre-collapse ruins have been found nearby. The mystery of the old world feels suddenly closer.
LanguageData.TN_Thought_EnvCatastropheNearby_Desc: A toxic event has contaminated land near our colony. The long-term effects are unknown.
LanguageData.TN_Thought_DroughtNearby_Desc: The skies are dry and the crops are barely growing. Every meal feels like it costs more than the last.
LanguageData.TN_TechBreakthroughVisitor_Body: A researcher connected to the breakthrough in {0} has arrived at the colony, seeking resources or shelter. They may be willing to share knowledge in exchange for support.
LanguageData.TN_AncientSiteSalvage_Body: A contact in {0} has forwarded a tip about the ancient site-along with a small cache of salvaged components ({1}x). More may follow if relations hold.
LanguageData.TN_AbandonedRuins_LootedLine: This site has already been picked over.
LanguageData.TN_Ruins_Scavenge_GizmoDesc: Spend a few hours searching the abandoned site for usable salvage. Yields a small cache of materials and leaves a grim impression on the caravan.
LanguageData.TN_Ruins_Scavenge_Confirm: Pick over the ruins of {0}? The salvage will be modest, and the caravan won't forget what they saw here.
LanguageData.TN_Ruins_Scavenge_Done: The caravan picked over the ruins of {0} and pulled what salvage they could from the wreckage.
LanguageData.TN_Thought_SawDeadCity_Desc: I helped pick over the bones of a city that died. There was nobody left to bury the dead. It is not the kind of thing you forget.
LanguageData.TN_QuestHook_War_Headline: Smugglers ask the colony to run aid through the blockade around {0}
LanguageData.TN_QuestHook_War_Body: A back-channel from {0} - believed routed by {1} - reaches the colony with a request: help move medicine and rations past the fighting. A caravan offer is on its way.
LanguageData.TN_QuestHook_War_Story: The war around {0} has closed the official trade routes. Smugglers, traders, and quiet diplomats are improvising. The colony's name has come up. The request was passed via what reads like {1}'s back channel - a careful, {2} ask, not a demand. "{3}" If the colony helps, it is a deliberate choice and will be remembered as such.
LanguageData.TN_QuestHook_Plague_Headline: Refugees fleeing the outbreak in {0} are being driven toward the colony
LanguageData.TN_QuestHook_Plague_Body: {1} confirms a group of refugees fleeing the outbreak in {0} is heading the colony's way - pursued by raiders. Expect arrivals within days.
LanguageData.TN_QuestHook_Plague_Story: The outbreak in {0} has done what outbreaks do: it has pushed people onto the roads. A group has been moving fast, pursued. {1}'s statement was {2} and to the point. "{3}" Whether the colony helps them quarantine, fight, or move on is a call only the colony can make - and the storyteller will keep score.
LanguageData.TN_QuestHook_Coup_Headline: A political asylum request lands near the colony from {0}
LanguageData.TN_QuestHook_Coup_Body: An escape pod is on a trajectory toward the colony's region. The brief frames it as a {1}-backed extraction tied to the unrest in {0}.
LanguageData.TN_QuestHook_Coup_Story: The coup in {0} has produced its share of fugitives. One has chosen - or been chosen - to head for the colony. The framing from {1} was {2} and not entirely forthcoming. "{3}" The pod will land soon. The decisions after that are the player's.
LanguageData.TN_QuestHook_Famine_Headline: A famine survivor walks out of {0} and asks for the colony
LanguageData.TN_QuestHook_Famine_Body: A lone wanderer from {0} is moving toward the colony. {1}'s council had no objection.
LanguageData.TN_QuestHook_Famine_Story: The famine in {0} has stripped settlements to the bone. A single survivor - described as resourceful, undeterred, and very hungry - is approaching the colony. {1}'s statement was unusually {2}, more permission than blessing. "{3}" The colony will decide whether to take them in when they arrive.
LanguageData.TN_RuinsRefugees_UnknownCity: a city whose name has been forgotten
LanguageData.TN_RuinsRefugees_Headline_Single: A survivor walks out of the ruins of {0}
LanguageData.TN_RuinsRefugees_Headline_Group: Refugees from the ruined city of {0} reach the region
LanguageData.TN_RuinsRefugees_Body_Single: Caravans report a lone figure on the regional roads - said to have left {0} after {1} stopped sending patrols.
LanguageData.TN_RuinsRefugees_Body_Group: A small band of survivors from the ruined city of {0} is reported moving through the region. {1} has lost contact with them.
LanguageData.TN_RuinsRefugees_Story: {0} stood as a settlement of {1} until {2} ended it. Reports now describe survivors finding their way to neighbouring regions - some alone, some in small groups, all carrying very little. They are not soldiers; they are people who walked out of a place that could no longer hold them. Whatever the colony decides when one of them arrives at the perimeter will be on the record.
LanguageData.TN_Flag_OpenConsoleGizmoDesc: Open the News Console and jump to the most recent report linked to this flag.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Phrase_Pragmatic_0: Patience is its own kind of strength.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Phrase_Pragmatic_1: We deal with what is, not what we wish for.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Phrase_Pragmatic_2: Cool heads keep the lights on.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Phrase_Pragmatic_3: Every decision has a price; we choose to know it.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Phrase_Pragmatic_4: Stability is built one quiet day at a time.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Phrase_Aggressive_0: We answer threats in the language they understand.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Phrase_Aggressive_1: Hesitation is a wound we will not give the enemy.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Phrase_Aggressive_2: Let them come; we are ready.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Phrase_Aggressive_3: Mercy is for those who have earned it.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Phrase_Aggressive_4: The strong protect the weak; the weak hide behind words.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Phrase_Zealot_0: The truth has chosen us, not the other way around.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Phrase_Zealot_1: Compromise is a slow form of surrender.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Phrase_Zealot_2: What we believe, we believe to the end.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Phrase_Zealot_3: Doubt is the work of those who have nothing to fight for.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Phrase_Zealot_4: History will remember which side we were on.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Bodyline: An untranslated coded broadcast cuts across the receiver's frequency band.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Story: The pattern repeats. There are no callsigns, no preambles, no end-of-message tags. It does not appear to be in any cipher used by the world's known factions. With the right decoder at the comms console, it may yield more - but the signal will not wait forever.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Fail_NoItem: Select a coded broadcast to decode.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Fail_NotCoded: This is not a coded broadcast.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Fail_AlreadyDecoded: This broadcast has already been decoded.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Fail_NotArrived: The broadcast has not finished receiving yet.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_DecodeButton_Tip: Use the comms console to decode this coded broadcast. The result is unpredictable. The signal may yield nothing of value - or it may not.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Decoded_NoRumor_Body: The decoded payload contains only routine signal traffic - no actionable intelligence.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Decoded_NoRumor_Story: Whoever sent it appears to have been calibrating their transmitters. Disappointing - but not every signal is meant to be heard.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Decoded_Rumor_Body: The decoded payload references a current rumor in your feed: "{0}".
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Decoded_Rumor_Story_Confi: The coded broadcast independently confirms the rumor "{0}". Whatever channel produced this message had access to the same source - and it considered the report accurate.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Decoded_Rumor_Story_False: The coded broadcast flatly contradicts the rumor "{0}". A correction has been issued. The rumor was wrong - whether from sloppy reporting or a deliberate planting is unknown.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Decoded_Cache_Uncommon_Bo: The decoded payload contains coordinates for a small abandoned cache. The marker is visible on your world map for {0} days.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Decoded_Cache_Uncommon_St: What waits at the site is unknown. The broadcast revealed the location - not whether anyone or anything is already there.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Decoded_Cache_Rare_Body: The decoded payload identifies a major cache - pre-collapse drop site or salvage stash. Marker is visible on the world map for {0} days.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Decoded_Cache_Rare_Story: A site like this would have been worth fighting over once. It may still be. Bring more than one rifle.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Decoded_Cache_Jackpot_Bod: The decoded payload identifies what appears to be a pre-collapse vault. The marker is visible on the world map for {0} days.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Decoded_Cache_Jackpot_Sto: Whatever was sealed inside has waited a long time for someone to come looking. So have whatever else is waiting with it.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Jackpot_LeadGranted: Vault records expose an intelligence lead against {0}. Your operatives can corroborate any rumor about them on sight for the next year.
LanguageData.TN_LootCache_Scavenge_GizmoDesc: Search this site for whatever the decoded broadcast pointed to. There is no way to tell from the world map what - or who - is there.
LanguageData.TN_LootCache_Scavenge_Confirm: Approach the cache coordinates and search the site?
LanguageData.TN_LootCache_Expired_Msg: A decoded cache signal has faded out before anyone reached it.
LanguageData.TN_LootCache_HostileMechs_Msg: Dormant mechanoids stir as the cache is breached. Your caravan fights through them.
LanguageData.TN_LootCache_HostileInsects_Msg: Sleeping insects boil out of the cache. Your caravan is forced to fight clear.
LanguageData.TN_LootCache_HostileRaiders_Msg: Raider squatters had moved in. Your caravan drives them off before stripping the site.
LanguageData.TN_LootCache_HostileManhunters_Msg: A manhunter pack had denned in the ruins. Your caravan beats them back to claim the cache.
LanguageData.TN_LootCache_CryostasisPawn_Found: Among the salvage your caravan finds a sealed cryptosleep casket. An occupant - {0} - sleeps inside.
LanguageData.TN_VerifyFail_CodedBroadcast: Coded broadcasts cannot be verified. Use the comms-console decoder instead.
LanguageData.TN_VerifyFail_Forecast: Future-dated bulletins cannot be verified. There is no source to cross-check against.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_Posted_LetterBody: The receiver has captured an untranslated coded broadcast - the entry has been logged in the News Console. With Signal Decoder research and a powered comms console, the broadcast can be decoded. Most decodes are routine. Some are not.
LanguageData.TN_NumbersFeed_CacheRevealed_LetterBody: The decoded broadcast has placed a marker on your world map. The signal will fade after roughly {0} days. What is at the site - and what may already be there - is unknown.
LanguageData.TN_WrongDateline_Posted_LetterBody: The receiver has logged a bulletin with a future dateline of {0}. Such items appear from time to time. On rare occasions the predicted event arrives on schedule. Most of the time, the date passes without incident. There is no way to tell which this is.
LanguageData.TN_WrongDateline_Body: The headline is dated {0}. This is in the future. Reception artefact, advance leak, or misprint - there is no way to be certain.
LanguageData.TN_WrongDateline_Story: The receiver flagged this broadcast as anomalous: its preamble carries a date that has not yet occurred. Such items appear from time to time, and on rare occasions the predicted event arrives precisely on schedule. Most of the time, the date passes without incident.
LanguageData.TN_WrongDateline_Confirmed_Body: An earlier broadcast carried a future date. The event it foretold has now occurred.
LanguageData.TN_WrongDateline_Confirmed_Story: The receiver appears to occasionally pick up bulletins shortly before they happen - through what mechanism is not known. The colony's records of past datelines are quietly amended.
LanguageData.TN_WrongDateline_Misprint_Body: An earlier broadcast carried a future date. The day has come and gone. Nothing happened.
LanguageData.TN_WrongDateline_Misprint_Story: Reception artefact, distant misprint, or something else entirely. Whoever sent it never sent the matching event.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableNumbersFeed_Tip: Very rarely (roughly once per quadrum, gated by reception), the receiver picks up an untranslated coded broadcast. With Signal Decoder research and a powered comms console, the broadcast can be decoded - most decodes confirm an existing rumor, but a small fraction reveal coordinates of an abandoned cache. Disabling this turns the numbers feed off entirely.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableWrongDateline_Tip: Once every 3-5 in-game years, the receiver picks up a bulletin dated in the future. The event it predicts may or may not actually occur - the dateline is not flagged as good or bad. Most are misprints; some are real. Disabling this prevents future-dated bulletins from posting.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableLiveIntercept_Tip: Every couple of weeks (gated by reception), a fugitive - a defector, a burned spy, a deposed minister - crosses the region on foot, moving toward safety. A marker travels the world map; race a caravan onto its tile to cut them off and choose to shelter, ransom, or rob them. Disabling this stops manhunts from spawning.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableColonistFame_Tip: When a colonist does something legendary - holds a line through hundreds of kills, breaks machine after machine, or cuts down a faction's leader - the wider world starts using their name. Deeds are always recorded; the colony only "becomes news" while a radio receiver is active. Disabling this stops renown from being tracked.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableColonistFameConsequenc: When on, renown and intercepts carry consequences: fame draws admirers who travel to join, infamy draws bounty hunters, and sheltering a fugitive from an already-hostile regime can bring pursuers. When off, these stay purely narrative and mood - no extra raids or visitors are queued.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableFactionPatrols_Tip: Factions send armed columns across the world map with a stated objective - a garrison sweep around one of their own towns, or a march toward the front during a war. You can watch them but not meet them. A hostile column straying near your colony can escalate into a raid; a friendly one within reach will break off to relieve your colony while it is under attack. Disabling this stops patrols and their consequences.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableFactionExpansion_Tip: Strong, aggressive powers occasionally found a brand-new settlement in wilderness near their capital, reported in the feed. Founding grows that faction's power, raises its perceived threat, and adds to its leader's legacy (a leader who keeps expanding can become known as "the Expander"). Rare and capped so the map stays recognisable. Relies on Faction Simulation being enabled to drive the power and threat that gate it. Disabling this stops new settlements from being founded.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnablePatrolAttacks_Tip: When on, a caravan that catches a faction patrol can attack it - the fight plays out on a generated battle map with your pawns under full control. Attacking is an act of war and turns that faction hostile. When off, patrols can only be observed.
LanguageData.TN_Patrol_AttackGizmoDesc: Fall on this {0} patrol with your caravan. The fight plays out on a generated map under your control. This is an act of war and will turn {0} hostile.
LanguageData.TN_Patrol_AttackConfirm: Attack the {0} patrol? Your caravan will fight them on a battle map. This is an act of war and will turn {0} hostile.
LanguageData.TN_Patrol_Engaged_Msg: Your caravan has engaged the {0} patrol.
LanguageData.TN_Patrol_Victory_Msg: Your caravan wiped out the {0} patrol.
LanguageData.TN_Patrol_Retreat_Msg: Your caravan broke off from the {0} patrol and withdrew.
LanguageData.TN_Patrol_Relief_Body: A nearby {0} patrol broke off and rushed to your colony's aid. {1} of their fighters have arrived to help drive off the attack.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_ShowWorldIncidentFlags: Show incident flags on the world map
LanguageData.TN_Settings_ShowWorldIncidentFlags_Tip: Pin small flags on affected faction settlements for active regional incidents (war, plague, coup, famine, environmental catastrophe, espionage, alliance, drought). You can also toggle this directly from the button on the world map's bottom-right control row.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_ShowCapitalCrowns: Show capital crowns on the world map
LanguageData.TN_Settings_ShowCapitalCrowns_Tip: Mark each faction's capital city with a crown icon next to its settlement on the world map. The capital is chosen once from terrain, roads, rivers and centrality, and moves only if the capital is destroyed or relocated.
LanguageData.TN_ToggleIncidentOverlay: The News: show world incident flags (war, plague, famine, …)
LanguageData.TN_Settings_IdeologyReactions_Tip: With Ideology active, colonists react to world events through the lens of their ideoligion: pacifists take distant wars harder, raider/supremacist cultures shrug them off, and nature-revering ideoligions are hit harder by environmental disasters. Purely a reaction-strength weighting; turning it off uses flat reactions.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_AnomalyBroadcasts_Tip: With Anomaly active, a small fraction of coded broadcasts arrive as distorted, unsettling "dead air" transmissions. Decoding them is mostly atmosphere, with a rare real lead. Disabling this keeps all coded broadcasts ordinary.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_RoyaltyDispatches_Tip: With Royalty active, news involving the Empire takes a royal tone, and colonies with a titled colonist can receive occasional court-intelligence dispatches. Disabling this uses neutral wording and no court channel.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_BiotechFlavor_Tip: With Biotech active, regional reports gain xenotype, sanguophage, and mechanoid-cluster flavor where relevant. Cosmetic only.
LanguageData.TN_AnomalyFeed_Bodyline: An intercept that should not be there. The carrier wave is wrong.
LanguageData.TN_AnomalyFeed_Story: The receiver locked onto something between the usual channels — a flat, breathing static with structure buried inside it. The operator says it does not behave like any faction cipher. It repeats, slightly different each time, as if it is listening back.
LanguageData.TN_AnomalyFeed_Posted_LetterBody: The radio has picked up a coded broadcast that does not match any known faction signal. It feels wrong. With Signal Decoder research and a powered comms console, you can attempt to decode it.
LanguageData.TN_AnomalyFeed_Decoded_Headline: Decoded: it was never meant for us
LanguageData.TN_AnomalyFeed_Decoded_Body: The signal resolves into something that is not language — and then, for one frame, into our colony's name.
LanguageData.TN_AnomalyFeed_Decoded_Story: Hours of work reduce the transmission to a single intelligible fragment, and the operators wish it had stayed noise. There are no coordinates, no faction, no demand. Just the sense of having been catalogued. The crew has agreed not to play it again.
LanguageData.TN_CourtIntel_Body0: A discreet channel relays the latest from {2}'s court.
LanguageData.TN_CourtIntel_Story0: {1}, {0} of the colony, receives a coded courtesy from old acquaintances at court: factions are realigning around the throne, favors are being called in, and a quiet reshuffle of titles is underway. None of it threatens the colony directly — but it pays to know which way the Empire is leaning.
LanguageData.TN_CourtIntel_Headline1: Court intelligence: edicts and undercurrents in {0}
LanguageData.TN_CourtIntel_Body1: {2}'s court has been busy, and word reaches the colony first.
LanguageData.TN_CourtIntel_Story1: Through {1}'s standing at court, the colony learns of fresh edicts and the gossip beneath them: a logistics decree dressed as ceremony, a rival's fall from favor, a permit that may soon be easier to obtain. The {0}'s contacts ask for nothing yet — only that the courtesy be remembered.
LanguageData.TN_CourtIntel_Headline2: Court intelligence: the throne's quiet business in {0}
LanguageData.TN_CourtIntel_Body2: A back-channel dispatch from {2}, for {1}'s eyes.
LanguageData.TN_CourtIntel_Story2: Being a {0} still opens doors. {1} is briefed on the throne's quiet business: troop rotations framed as honor guards, a succession whisper that refuses to die, and which border holdings the Empire now considers expendable. Useful context the open broadcasts will not carry for weeks.
LanguageData.TN_Biotech_Body0: An unusual migration is reported near {0}.
LanguageData.TN_Biotech_Story0: Travelers describe a column moving through {0} unlike the usual trade caravans — a mix of xenotypes keeping to themselves, well-armed and unhurried. Where they are bound, nobody will say. Such migrations sometimes scatter new arrivals toward distant colonies in the months that follow.
LanguageData.TN_Biotech_Body1: A cluster's transponder chatter has been picked up around {0}.
LanguageData.TN_Biotech_Story1: The receiver catches the cold, repeating handshake of a mechanoid cluster somewhere near {0}. It is not moving toward anyone yet. Operators log the bearing and note that clusters which go quiet have a habit of reappearing closer than expected.
LanguageData.TN_Biotech_Body2: Hushed accounts of a deathless visitor circulate around {0}.
LanguageData.TN_Biotech_Story2: A trader swears that a guest in {0} did not eat, did not age, and left before dawn. Most dismiss it as drink and superstition — but the older hands grow quiet, and the colony's medic asks, a little too casually, how the story ended.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_IronGeneral_Phrase1: Hold the line, or become it.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Warhawk_Phrase0: Peace is the pause between victories.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Warhawk_Phrase2: Every border is a question of will.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Conqueror_Phrase0: What is held is what is owned.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Conqueror_Phrase1: The map is redrawn by those who dare.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Butcher_Phrase0: I do not count the dead. I count the surrendered.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Butcher_Phrase2: They will remember what defiance costs.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Reaver_Phrase0: Take fast, leave nothing, owe no one.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Reaver_Phrase1: The strong eat; the slow are eaten.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Reaver_Phrase2: We do not negotiate with cargo.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Strongman_Phrase0: Order is whatever I say it is.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Strongman_Phrase1: Loyalty is rewarded; doubt is not.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Strongman_Phrase2: A firm hand steadies a shaking world.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Marauder_Phrase0: The frontier belongs to whoever takes it.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Marauder_Phrase1: Walls invite us; they do not stop us.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Reformer_Phrase0: Change what you can; survive the rest.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Reformer_Phrase1: Better a slow road than a cliff.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Reformer_Phrase2: Reputation is a resource; spend it wisely.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_MerchantPrince_Phrase0: Every quarrel is a market closed.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_MerchantPrince_Phrase2: A signed ledger outlives any banner.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Broker_Phrase0: There is always a deal nobody has named yet.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Broker_Phrase1: I trade in outcomes, not grudges.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Broker_Phrase2: Talk is the cheapest weapon I own.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Steward_Phrase1: Tend the people and the people endure.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Steward_Phrase2: Waste nothing — least of all goodwill.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Technocrat_Phrase0: Sentiment is noise; data is signal.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Technocrat_Phrase1: Fix the system, not the blame.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Peacemaker_Phrase0: No enemy is permanent who can still be fed.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Peacemaker_Phrase1: Lower the spears; raise the question.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Peacemaker_Phrase2: I would rather be owed than feared.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Administrator_Phrase0: Stability is a habit, not an event.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Administrator_Phrase1: Quiet borders are the truest victory.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_PriestKing_Phrase0: The faithful do not bargain with the fallen.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_PriestKing_Phrase1: Doctrine is the only border that matters.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_PriestKing_Phrase2: We answer to a higher ledger than yours.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Prophet_Phrase0: I have seen the end of your patience.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Prophet_Phrase1: Heed the sign, or become one.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Prophet_Phrase2: The world is a sermon written in ash.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Inquisitor_Phrase1: Confession first; mercy is discussed later.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Inquisitor_Phrase2: Doubt is the disease; I am the cure.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Purifier_Phrase0: What cannot be cleansed is cut away.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Purifier_Phrase1: The flame remembers what the flesh forgets.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Purifier_Phrase2: A pure people needs no neighbors.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Hierophant_Phrase0: The unworthy are not told the hour.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Hierophant_Phrase1: Silence is the speech of the chosen.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Hierophant_Phrase2: We outlast empires by ignoring them.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Doomsayer_Phrase0: Count your harvests; they are numbered.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Doomsayer_Phrase1: The reckoning does not take appointments.
LanguageData.TN_Persona_Doomsayer_Phrase2: I do not threaten. I forecast.
LanguageData.TN_Intercept_Inspect_Heading: A fugitive ({0}) is crossing the region.
LanguageData.TN_Intercept_Inspect_Window: Window to intercept: about {0}d {1}h before they reach safety.
LanguageData.TN_Intercept_CaughtUp: Your caravan has caught up with the fugitive. Select the caravan to act.
LanguageData.TN_Intercept_GizmoDesc: Cut off the fugitive crossing this tile and decide what to do with them.
LanguageData.TN_Intercept_Opt_Shelter: Shelter them (they join you; they talk)
LanguageData.TN_Intercept_Opt_Rob: Take what they carry and leave them
LanguageData.TN_Intercept_Letter_Body: {0} is fleeing {1} and crossing the region near you. There are roughly {2} days to reach them with a caravan before they slip away. Find them on the world map.
LanguageData.TN_Intercept_Robbed_Msg: Took {0} silver from the fugitive and left them on the road.
LanguageData.TN_Intercept_Escaped_Msg: {0} reached safety. The trail is cold.
LanguageData.TN_Intercept_Debrief_Intro: {0} settled into the colony and told your people what they knew about {1}.
LanguageData.TN_Intercept_Debrief_Rumors: They corroborated {0} standing report(s) on the feed — open rumors about {1} are now resolved as confirmed or exposed as false.
LanguageData.TN_Intercept_Debrief_NoRumors: There were no open rumors about {0} for them to settle right now.
LanguageData.TN_Intercept_Debrief_RevealTrue: Most usefully, they confirmed the truth behind the {0}: the stated cause — {1} — is genuine. It will now read as certain on the feed.
LanguageData.TN_Intercept_Debrief_RevealFalse: Most usefully, they exposed the {0} for what it is: the official cause — {1} — is a cover story. The feed will now flag it as such.
LanguageData.TN_Intercept_Debrief_NoThread: {0} has no major movement brewing that they could shed light on right now.
LanguageData.TN_Thought_Celebrity_Desc: The whole region is saying my name. It is a strange and heady thing to be a legend.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableInterventions_Tip: Let your comms actions (Aid the Besieged, Request Ceasefire, Support Regime) push real war and faction outcomes, then report back days later what your intervention actually did — including when it wasn't enough.
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_DisabledInSettings: Interventions are disabled in mod settings.
LanguageData.TN_Settings_EnableStandingGate_Tip: Weigh your interventions against the colony's strength and reputation. A small, unloved colony that tries to broker ceasefires, back regimes, or send aid may be publicly rebuffed — a goodwill hit and a mocking item in the feed — instead of getting its way. Covert ops grow likelier to fail, and a diplomat's goodwill gains shrink. Turn this off to restore the old always-succeeds behaviour.
LanguageData.TN_InterventionFail_RebuffCooldown: {0} is still smarting from your last approach — give it time.
LanguageData.TN_AidBesieged_Tip: Ship medicine and rations to the losing side of this war. Buys them a bounded swing in momentum and slower exhaustion — enough to tip a close fight, never enough to reverse a rout. A follow-up report will tell you whether it worked. Costs 12 medicine and 20 meals; requires a powered comms console.
LanguageData.TN_WarReliefFail_RequiresRealisticWars: War relief requires realistic wars to be enabled.
LanguageData.TN_WarReliefFail_NoThread: No report chain is attached to this report.
LanguageData.TN_WarReliefFail_AlreadySent: Relief has already been sent for this war.
LanguageData.TN_WarReliefFail_NoBesiegedSide: Neither side is clearly losing yet — there is no one to relieve.
LanguageData.TN_WarReliefFail_NoHomeMap: No home colony to send relief from.
LanguageData.TN_WarRelief_Sent_Bodyline: Your colony has dispatched medicine and rations to {0}, besieged by {1}.
LanguageData.TN_WarRelief_Sent_Story: A relief shipment — {2} medicine and {3} meals — is on its way to {0}, hard-pressed in the war with {1}. Whether it reaches the front in time to matter is out of your hands now. Watch for word of what it changes.
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_WarRelief_Tipped_Body: Your shipment reached {0} in time; their front against {1} has stabilized.
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_WarRelief_Tipped_Story: FOLLOW-UP: The medicine and rations you sent to {0} arrived at the breaking point. Field reports credit the outside relief with steadying the line — {1}'s advance has stalled, and {0} still holds. Your colony's name travels with the convoy.
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_WarRelief_Insufficient_B: Your shipment reached {0}, but {1} broke through anyway.
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_WarRelief_Insufficient_S: FOLLOW-UP: The relief you sent bought {0} days, not victory. {1}'s offensive was too far advanced; the front broke despite the medicine and rations. What you sent was swallowed by the collapse — but the gesture was not forgotten.
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_WarRelief_Unresolved_Bod: Your shipment keeps {0} in the fight against {1}; the outcome is still undecided.
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_WarRelief_Unresolved_Sto: FOLLOW-UP: Weeks on, the war between {0} and {1} grinds without resolution. Your relief is part of what keeps {0} standing — the convoy's supplies are still being counted at the front. How it ends is anyone's guess.
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_Ceasefire_Tipped_Headlin: The guns fall silent between {0} and {1}
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_Ceasefire_Tipped_Body: Your ceasefire pressure told; {0} and {1} have laid down arms in an exhausted peace.
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_Ceasefire_Tipped_Story: FOLLOW-UP: The war-weariness your intercession pressed on both sides finally cracked the will to fight. {0} and {1} have settled into a white peace — no victor, no conquest, just two spent armies standing down. The channels remember who pushed for it.
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_Ceasefire_Insufficient_H: War outlasts your ceasefire call between {0} and {1}
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_Ceasefire_Insufficient_B: Despite your appeal, one side pressed its advantage to a decision.
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_Ceasefire_Insufficient_S: FOLLOW-UP: Your ceasefire request slowed neither side for long. The war between {0} and {1} ran to a decision on the battlefield rather than at the table. Some fights simply have to burn out.
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_Ceasefire_Unresolved_Hea: Ceasefire call hangs unanswered — {0} and {1} fight on
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_Ceasefire_Unresolved_Bod: The belligerents have neither made peace nor forced a decision.
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_Ceasefire_Unresolved_Sto: FOLLOW-UP: Weeks after your ceasefire request, {0} and {1} are still at each other's throats — neither exhausted enough to quit nor strong enough to win. The appeal sits on the record, unanswered.
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_SupportRegime_Tipped_Bod: Your backing helped {0}'s leadership weather the coup.
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_SupportRegime_Tipped_Sto: FOLLOW-UP: The coup against {0}'s leadership has collapsed, and the ruling faction survives. Observers credit a mix of loyalty, luck, and the outside backing you pledged — how much your support tipped the balance, no one can say for certain. Either way, the regime remembers who stood by it.
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_SupportRegime_Insufficie: Your backing was not enough; {0}'s leadership has been swept aside.
FOLLOW-UP: For all the support you pledged, the coup in {0} succeeded. Power has changed hands. Your bet on the old order did not pay — though those who remember it may yet return the favor.
LanguageData.TN_Intervention_SupportRegime_Unresolved: The coup in {0} has neither succeeded nor been put down.

FOLLOW-UP: Long after your pledge of support, {0}'s fate is still contested. The coup has not been crushed, nor has it toppled the regime. Your backing is one weight on a scale that has not yet tipped.
